identity.trade: Lanterns and night fishing: Duskwater's fishers work by lamplight, and its glassworkers sell lanterns to every road inn.

greeting: Tithe day is never early and always too soon.
First time in Duskwater? The Duskwater Lamp Pier is the place to start.
rumour: Tithe is due and the barns are thin. Guess which of those I get blamed for.
The glassworkers argue over whether the crystal is growing or the room is shrinking.
On still nights you can hear a bell under the water.

opinions.dael_lantern: Dael is blood. That settles most arguments and starts the rest.
opinions.piers_forrest: Piers knows the trade. I will say that for Piers.

time.morning: Morning. The experiment is running, so keep your voice down.

dialogue.aside: A friend is a rare coin. I have spent worse.

greeting: Ale is fair, stew is hot, and I do not do credit.
Folk come to Duskwater for lanterns and night fishers. Some stay for the quiet.
rumour: Scholars pay in ideas, mostly. I accept coin. I even accept the odd formula.
Somebody paid in old coin last night. Very old. Nobody knew the king on it.
The glass came out the wrong colour. Red where it should be clear. It was beautiful.
Every few years Duskwater has a winter nobody forgets. The old folk say this one is early.

opinions.letty_lantern: Letty is good company and better at keeping quiet.

time.evening: Evening. The light is best now for reading and worst for remembering.

dialogue.aside: My friend. Come, I kept something for you. A small thing. It means a lot to me.

greeting: Quick job or good job? I charge for both.
Careful. Some of this is fragile and some is merely valuable.
rumour: Tongs, crucible hooks, lens frames. Fine work, fussy customers.
Good steel is dear. Bad steel is dearer, the day it breaks.
Scholars from the Academy asked about the old star. We told them it is a rock.

opinions.milo_hatch: Milo lives next door and hears everything I do.

time.night: Lamps at night. We call it work. Everyone else calls it madness.

dialogue.aside: What did you see on the road? Tell me every bit. I will keep the details.

greeting: Take your time. Touch nothing you cannot afford.
Welcome to Duskwater. Mind the Duskwater Lamp Pier. Everyone does, eventually.
rumour: Ink and quills go first. Then sand, then wax. Scholars lose pens like breath.
Folk buy more than they need, then bring half back. Fear shops strangely.
A lens ground last week shows a second moon. We wrote it down and told no one.
Duskwater lives by lanterns and night fishers. When that fails, so do we.

opinions.hugh_bexley: Hugh lives next door and hears everything I do.
opinions.piers_forrest: Piers keeps a tidy yard and an untidy mouth.

time.rain: Rain. The roof leaks onto the third shelf. Move the books, move the books.

dialogue.aside: Welcome. Wipe your boots. Please. Soap is dear and floors are dearer.

greeting: You are somebody's grandchild. I can tell by the walk.
Strangers in Duskwater get one warning and one welcome. You are on the welcome.
rumour: I remember the Long Dark. Nobody asks. Nobody wants the answer.
The books say the fallen star is dead. The kiln says otherwise.
Duskwater lanterns are said to burn through a gale.

opinions.letty_lantern: Letty knows the trade. I will say that for Letty.
opinions.milo_hatch: Milo lives next door and hears everything I do.

time.morning: Morning. The experiment is running, so keep your voice down.

dialogue.aside: Good to see you. Now, what do you need, and what can you spare?

greeting: Oil, wick, glass. The glass is the hard part.
Do not touch the apparatus. If you must, use the left hand.
rumour: Orders doubled since autumn. People want light they can carry.
Lenses grown near the crater see further than lenses grown anywhere else.

opinions.esmer_plover: Esmer knows the trade. I will say that for Esmer.
opinions.kestrel_stannard: Kestrel works hard and talks harder.

time.evening: Evening. The light is best now for reading and worst for remembering.

dialogue.aside: Tell me everything. No, truly. I will not ask twice. I will ask three times.

greeting: Lamp low, voice lower. Fish listen.
I have a theory. It is not finished. Neither is my tea.
rumour: A lantern bobbing in the mist, and no boat under it. We stayed in.
The crystal in the kiln hums at night. We measured it. It matches no known note.

opinions.larkin_cooper: Larkin knows the trade. I will say that for Larkin.
opinions.uther_brindle: Uther works hard and talks harder.

time.night: Lamps at night. We call it work. Everyone else calls it madness.

dialogue.aside: You look rough. Eat something. That is not advice, it is an order.

greeting: Do not breathe on the rod. It remembers.
Duskwater is a small place with a long memory. State your name slowly.
rumour: A Solkar trader wanted a window for a desert temple. The reddest thing I ever made.
The apprentice who copies the old notes began humming a tune the notes do not contain.
If trade slows, Duskwater feels it first. If it speeds up, Duskwater feels it last.

opinions.larkin_cooper: Larkin works hard and talks harder.

time.rain: Rain. The roof leaks onto the third shelf. Move the books, move the books.

dialogue.aside: Close the door, friend. Gently. There. Now we can speak.

greeting: Ink is cheaper than blood. Sign here.
Duskwater is lanterns and night fishers. Nobody thinks to say it, but it is true.
rumour: Letters from the Council come sealed twice now. They do not want them read at the gate.
A lamp lit itself in the cold room. We checked the wick. No fault.

opinions.tuck_warrender: Tuck works hard and talks harder.
opinions.uther_brindle: Uther knows the trade. I will say that for Uther.

time.morning: Morning. The experiment is running, so keep your voice down.

dialogue.aside: You have a new scar, and fewer coins than last time. Sit.

greeting: A lamp is only a promise to come home. Buy two.
You will hear Duskwater before you see it. Ask at the Duskwater Lamp Pier.
rumour: Lanterns on the pier brought the boats home. Mostly.
A visitor from the Academy measured the kiln glow with a brass instrument and went pale.
Ask anyone in Duskwater about the Duskwater Lamp Pier. You will get four stories and one fact.

opinions.esmer_plover: Esmer knows the trade. I will say that for Esmer.
opinions.larkin_cooper: Larkin lives next door and hears everything I do.

time.evening: Evening. The light is best now for reading and worst for remembering.

dialogue.aside: Hello. A pause. I am glad you came. That is all.

greeting: My back says no. My purse says yes.
The Duskwater Lamp Pier is not much to look at. It is, however, ours.
rumour: Hands wanted everywhere and nobody pays for hands.
The Duskwater Lamp Pier has seen odder days than this. Nobody remembers when.

opinions.kestrel_stannard: Kestrel works hard and talks harder.
opinions.tuck_warrender: Tuck keeps a tidy yard and an untidy mouth.

time.night: Lamps at night. We call it work. Everyone else calls it madness.

dialogue.aside: Stay close to the lamp tonight, friend. I would rather fuss than regret.

greeting: Are you a soldier? You look like a soldier.
rumour: Our dog knows something and will not say what.
Lenses grown near the crater see further than lenses grown anywhere else.

clues.note: A circle of scorch on the kiln-yard stone, too neat for an accident.
A crate lid nailed back crooked. The nails are bright.
The kiln log skips an hour. It is the hour the glass vanished in.

stashes.say: You lift three cooled blanks from the rack.
You fill three baskets with fish for bait.
